classification.difficultyReason: Express adjacent coefficients with an unknown expansion power and simplify their factorial and numerical-power ratios to obtain an equation for n.

content.prompt: In the expansion of $(3+2x)^n$, the coefficients of $x^5$ and $x^6$ are equal. Find the value of $n$.

answer.worked:
$$T_k=\binom{n}{k}3^{n-k}2^kx^k.$$
The coefficients of $x^5$ and $x^6$ are equal:
$$\begin{align*}\binom{n}{5}3^{n-5}2^5&=\binom{n}{6}3^{n-6}2^6\\3&=2\frac{\binom{n}{6}}{\binom{n}{5}}.\end{align*}$$
Using factorials,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\binom{n}{6}}{\binom{n}{5}}&=\frac{n!}{6!(n-6)!}\frac{5!(n-5)!}{n!}\\\frac{\binom{n}{6}}{\binom{n}{5}}&=\frac{n-5}{6}\\3&=\frac{2(n-5)}{6}\\18&=2(n-5)\\n&=14.\end{align*}$$
